parts.text: Around the country, other collections also exist, including of arthropods and

as well as the Allan Herbarium at the Bioeconomy Science Institute. The University of Otago’s geology museum is an example of a collection held by an academic institution.

But these collections aren’t protected by an act of parliament like Te Papa, and they don’t have the same level of public

or funding the national museum has. I propose they should all be combined to form the basis of a new museum.

Current public displays on New Zealand’s biodiversity don’t always put it into a global or evolutionary

. For example, New Zealand is the cradle of penguin evolution and the ancestors of many now endemic birds came from Australia, South America, the northern hemisphere and in some cases, places unknown.

Biodiversity displays could be further

by showcasing New Zealand’s geological heritage. Rock and mineral displays can be popular attractions and it would be a prime opportunity to put pounamu in a global context. Pounamu is the Indigenous Māori name for nephrite jade and

, which is a taonga (treasure) for carving.

From contested to globally relevant spaces

The Victorian concept of a museum has a colonial history. This has led to collections containing numerous contested objects such as the Parthenon

in the British Museum and Indigenous human remains stored in collections worldwide.

By being open about this history and working with mana whenua (local Māori groups), a new museum could help heal these rifts.

This would enable

with a global focus, for example about the evolution of life on Earth, to be told through the fossil record and living biodiversity.

A prime example is the fossil of one of the first dinosaurs ever described (Iguanodon), held by Te Papa, which helped start the world’s

interest in dinosaurs.

Currently Te Papa does not display any biodiversity from outside New Zealand. Imagine seeing a whole gallery of fossil and living whale skeletons to illustrate their remarkable evolutionary

from land to sea, similar to displays in the gallery of palaeontology and comparative anatomy in Paris.

Like the incredible, almost complete Triceratops skeleton Museums Victoria acquired for AU$3 million, a dedicated
history museum in New Zealand should source specimens and loans ethically to promote collaborative research and public outreach.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: New Zealand's distinctive natural history makes a case for a museum devoted to evolution and geology.
Individual skin conditions change how perfume molecules evaporate and how a fragrance smells.
A compass works by aligning a magnetised needle with Earth's magnetic field.
Aboriginal astronomical knowledge explains celestial movements and their connections to life on Earth.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Like the Galapagos Islands, New Zealand’s unique isolation makes it an iconic natural history location of global importance.

questions.prompt: What would a dedicated New Zealand natural history museum celebrate?
options: The country's biodiversity, geology and fossil record
Exclusively the latest consumer electronics
Only the history of international banking
A complete collection of every European painting
questions.explanation: 第 4 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: I often wonder why New Zealand doesn’t have a dedicated natural history museum (like those in London, Paris, Vienna or New York) to celebrate its unique biodiversity, geology and fossil record.
